How much is carpet installation in Redmond, WA?

Plan on $4–$7 per square foot installed in Redmond, which covers carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. In practice, a single bedroom lands around $600–$1,000, a straight staircase around $235–$400, and a typical multi-room project around $2,400–$3,900. The biggest lever is carpet grade — and you set it yourself, comparing samples on your own floor during the free measure.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come to Redmond?

Yes — Redmond is core territory for us. The van arrives with 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades, we lay them in the rooms being carpeted so the color reads in your real light, then measure every room and stair. You get a written price before the visit ends, the visit is free, and evening and Saturday slots make it easy to schedule around a workday of calls.
What does carpet stretching cost in Redmond?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Redmond, and most rooms fall in the $99–$180 range. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and doorway humps flat again for roughly a fifth of what new carpet costs — so if the pile still stands up and the color still works, stretching is usually the right call.
What do carpeted stairs cost in Redmond?

Stair installation starts at $18 per step in waterfall or cap-and-band style, and a typical straight Redmond staircase totals $235–$400. Landings and pie-shaped winders go into the written quote at the measure — the number you approve is the number you pay.
How long will my Redmond carpet installation take?

One day, for most Redmond homes. A few bedrooms and a staircase is a routine single day for the crew; a full house with heavy furniture can spill into a second. If you work from home, tell us — we sequence the rooms so your office is emptied and back together first, and the schedule goes on your quote.
Will the installers move my furniture?

Yes — beds, couches, dressers and tables are included on most Redmond jobs, and everything goes back where it started. We ask you to handle the small and fragile things yourself: closet floors, electronics, monitors and anything with a cable you'd rather unplug personally.
Should I restretch my carpet or just replace it?

Restretch when the pile still stands, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that's a $99-per-room repair instead of a full replacement. Replace when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are letting go, the backing is crumbling, or pet odor has outlived a professional cleaning. We diagnose it honestly before quoting, because the wrong answer wastes your money either way.
Which Redmond neighborhoods do you cover?

All of them — Downtown Redmond, Education Hill, Grass Lawn, Overlake, Idylwood, Viewpoint, Sammamish Valley, Bear Creek, North Redmond, English Hill, Willows/Rose Hill and Southeast Redmond, plus Redmond Ridge, Union Hill and Novelty Hill just east of the city. The wider Eastside and Seattle are in range too.
Which carpet survives pets best?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, installed over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber tolerates strong cleaners without losing color. With Marymoor's off-leash park minutes away, it's the setup we quote most often in Redmond. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty comes with the installation?

OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet carries the mill's own warranty on top — usually 10 to 25 years against wear and staining, depending on grade. Both go on your written quote. Some mill warranties require a minimum pad grade, which is one more reason all three grades come along on the visit.
